data.title: Prosné – Zlatý kôň, a fortlet of the Púchov culture
data.excerpt: East of Prosné in the valley of the Marikovský potok, on a sharp mountain ridge, stood a small fortlet of the Púchov culture with intensive occupation around the turn of the 1st century BC and the 1st century AD. Its name, the Golden Horse, comes from an oral tradition about a hoard of gold coins bearing the image of a little horse that was said to have been found here.
data.metaTitle: Prosné – Zlatý kôň, a Púchov culture fortlet
data.metaDescription: The Zlatý kôň fortlet at Prosné in the valley of the Marikovský potok, a village that in the period of the Púchov culture had great cult significance.

children.text: From the previous article about the Celtic sacrificial site at the locality known as

we know that the village of Prosné, which lies in the valley of the Marikovský potok stream, apparently had great cult significance in the period of the Púchov culture. In this village, however, we also know of a very interesting hillfort called Zlatý kôň. I am glad to be able to bring you a short text about this hillfort together with pictures taken from the excellent (officially unpublished) set of documents entitled Po stopách predkov. The text is from the pen of Štefan Meliš and Jozef Moravčík, the photographs of the finds by Mr Martin Olšovský.

The second important site is the fortlet of the Púchov culture in the locality known as Zlatý kôň, which lies east of the village on a sharp mountain ridge, where there is a small fortification with intensive occupation from the turn of the 1st century BC and the 1st century AD.
A detailed survey of the site made it possible to identify, besides sherds, several iron objects as well – brooches, an arrowhead, nails, a belt clasp, small mounts and a small cramp.

A gold Celtic (?) coin is also said to have been found at this site (J. Chmulík), but it came into the hands of a goldsmith in Považská Bystrica. According to the finder’s description it bore a relief mark in the shape of a Z, which could be the stylised body of a little horse (?). Today this find can no longer be verified and more precisely identified. According to oral tradition, other gold coins – a whole hoard – are supposed to have been found here long ago, on which a little horse was said to be depicted (hence also the name Zlatý kôň, the Golden Horse), and with this hoard the finder is said to have bought the nearby clearing of Uhry.

children.text: Several legends about this site are handed down in the surrounding villages. According to one of them, the image of a ram was once supposedly carved into the rock below the summit. The legend may be right, but it was more likely the image of a horse. For the horse was a venerated animal among the Celts. An enormous silhouette of a horse carved on the side of a rocky hill is also to be found in England. On the summit of Zlatý kôň there is a narrow terrace on which there was a small fortlet, probably in the La Tène to Roman period. The fortlet was discovered by Štefan Meliš, who obtained several sherds there, sometime around 1962. According to Dr Petrovský-Šichman there was a Celtic cult place here. He sought the original name of the hill Zlatý kôň in connection with the folk tale about the Sun’s Horse. In the period of the “First” Republic two boys from Prosné found a coin, probably Celtic, near the fortlet and sold it to a goldsmith in Považská Bystrica.

Martin Olšovský, Štefan Meliš, Jozef Moravčík: Po stopách predkov, Archeológia Stredného Považia od praveku po stredovek – a set of documents and photographs, published by Martin Olšovský at his own expense in 2008 in an edition of 4 copies.
In December 2021 our Hradiská civic association, together with the Trenčín Museum, carried out an excavation of the fortlet.
Here you will find some of the finds from the excavation.
